  "reference_events": [
    {
      "event_id": "ref_fork_opening",
      "role": "fork_opening",
      "description": "Helicase uses ATP hydrolysis to open the DNA helix, forming a local replication fork with separated leading and lagging templates.",
      "evidence_ids": ["E_d8ffea5a5785"],
      "quote": "A helicase using the energy from ATP hydrolysis opens up the DNA helix. Replication forks are formed at each replication origin as the DNA unwinds."
    },
    {
      "event_id": "ref_rna_priming",
      "role": "rna_priming",
      "description": "Primase synthesizes RNA primers; DNA polymerase can then begin synthesis. Pol α adds a short DNA fragment to the primer on both strands before handoff.",
      "evidence_ids": ["E_d8ffea5a5785"],
      "quote": "Primers are formed by the enzyme primase, and using the primer, DNA pol can start synthesis. Three major DNA polymerases are then involved: α, δ and ε. DNA pol α adds a short (20 to 30 nucleotides) DNA fragment to the RNA primer on both strands, and then hands off to a second polymerase."
    },
    {
      "event_id": "ref_leading_synthesis",
      "role": "leading_strand_synthesis",
      "description": "Pol ε continuously synthesizes the leading strand.",
      "evidence_ids": ["E_d8ffea5a5785"],
      "quote": "While the leading strand is continuously synthesized by the enzyme pol ε , the lagging strand is synthesized by pol δ ."
    },
    {
      "event_id": "ref_lagging_synthesis",
      "role": "lagging_strand_synthesis",
      "description": "Pol δ synthesizes the lagging strand in short stretches (Okazaki fragments), each initiated by a separate primer.",
      "evidence_ids": ["E_d8ffea5a5785"],
      "quote": "the lagging strand is synthesized by pol δ ."
    },
    {
      "event_id": "ref_lagging_primers",
      "role": "lagging_strand_synthesis",
      "description": "On the lagging strand, DNA synthesis occurs in short stretches each initiated by a separate primer.",
      "evidence_ids": ["E_d8ffea5a5785"],
      "quote": "On the lagging strand, DNA is synthesized in short stretches, each of which is initiated by a separate primer."
    },
    {
      "event_id": "ref_primer_displacement",
      "role": "primer_replacement",
      "description": "As Pol δ encounters the RNA primer on the lagging strand, it displaces the primer from the DNA template.",
      "evidence_ids": ["E_d8ffea5a5785"],
      "quote": "As pol δ runs into the primer RNA on the lagging strand, it displaces it from the DNA template."
    },
    {
      "event_id": "ref_primer_removal",
      "role": "primer_replacement",
      "description": "The displaced RNA primer is removed by RNase H (also called flap endonuclease) and replaced with DNA nucleotides.",
      "evidence_ids": ["E_d8ffea5a5785"],
      "quote": "The displaced primer RNA is then removed by RNase H (AKA flap endonuclease ) and replaced with DNA nucleotides."
    },
    {
      "event_id": "ref_okazaki_joining",
      "role": "nick_sealing",
      "description": "Okazaki fragments are joined after RNA primers are replaced with DNA.",
      "evidence_ids": ["E_d8ffea5a5785"],
      "quote": "The Okazaki fragments in the lagging strand are joined after the replacement of the RNA primers with DNA."
    },
    {
      "event_id": "ref_ligase_sealing",
      "role": "nick_sealing",
      "description": "DNA ligase seals remaining gaps by forming phosphodiester bonds.",
      "evidence_ids": ["E_d8ffea5a5785"],
      "quote": "The gaps that remain are sealed by DNA ligase, which forms the phosphodiester bond."
    }
  ]
}
